sources.citation: Daniels, Don. Curriculum Vitae (Sept. 2021) and web page 'Manat', https://dondaniels.weebly.com/manat.html
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not a description; used to enumerate Daniels' Sogeram/Manat publications (2010 OL article, 2015 dissertation, 2020 De Gruyter book, PARADISEC collection DD1). Web page gives ~50 speakers in Paynamar and Simbevi, fieldwork 2010/2012/2014; no phonology.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don Roger. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 1127 pp. (eScholarship ark:/13030/qt1kj4174g). Appendix 2 'Manat Grammar Sketch', pp. 537-657; Manat phonology = section 2.2, pp. 542-549 (PDF pp. 567-574); ch. 2 section 2.3.2 'Manat Innovations', pp. 82-84.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Manat: section 2.2 covers consonant and vowel inventories, evidence for phonemic /ɨ/, phonotactics, morphophonemics (vowel elision, epenthesis, root vowel harmony) and word-initial vowel loss, with no mention of stress, accent, tone or prosody; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the 121-page sketch. The only stress remark in the entire dissertation is on p. 71 (Mand sound changes): 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.'

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: ANU. xvi+113 pp. (Paynamar = language H5).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: introduction (pp. viii-x) says transcription is 'semi-phonemic' and lists fluctuating sounds per language (Paynamar: a bilabial fricative ~ p); no stress marking convention or stress statement; wordlist only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. Section 2.22.43 'The Paynamar Language' and 2.22.45 'Typological features of the Wanang Stock', pp. 63-64.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: ten typological features (stop/nasal/fricative places, prenasalized voiced stops, high central vowel, no noun number, no concord classes, verb suffixes) with no mention of stress.
